{{nihongo|'''Tatenui Shrine (Miho, Ibaraki)'''|楯縫神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

'''Tatenui Shrine'' (Tatenui Shrine) is located at 2988 Gochu <ref>[http://www.oyashiro.or.jp/ According to the shrine register of the Ibaraki Prefectural Shrine Office, it is 2988 Kihara, Miura Village. </ref><ref name="1300kinen" /> (formerly {{ill|Shida district|Q11386034|qid=Q11386034}}{{ill|Kihara|Q11518209|qid=Q11518209}}) {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}}. The old name was {{ill|Shida district|Q11386034|qid=Q11386034}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi-sha}} ({{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}} Shinta District, small shrine). Former {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}}. There is also Tatenui Shrine with the same name in Shinta Miura Village.

=== Overview ===
[[File:Tatenui Shrine (Gochu, Miura Village, Ibaraki Prefecture) 03.jpg|thumb|First Torii]]
[[File:Tatenui-jinja shrine Ni no Torii Gate (Miho village, Ibaraki prefecture).jpg|thumb|Ni no Torii Gate]]
[[File:Tatenui Shrine (Gochu, Miura Village, Ibaraki Prefecture) 02.jpg|thumb|Chozusha]]
The approach road faces the {{ill|Japan National Route 125|Q6156756|qid=Q6156756}} existing road, but the shrine grounds are located in a secluded area and are difficult to find. A long approach path passes through a forest of giant trees, and the shrine building is located at the back. There are no shrine offices or prominent shrines within the precincts, so you can enjoy the simple composition of the grove of trees and shrine buildings.The precincts are designated by Ibaraki Prefecture {{ill|Nature Conservation Area|Q11612866|qid=Q11612866}} (29, Ichinomiya). {{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}} Fudu myth in the Shinta district section<ref>The original text of Hitachikuni Fudoki is ``Takakiri, Koroi, Tenchi Kinkoshi, Plants and trees language no time, the name of the deity who descended from heaven, the title '''Futu Great God''', Junko Ashihara Nakatsukuni, Hehei Mountain River Arakyo no Rui, Great God Transformation Dojinbi, Mind Returns to Heaven, Immediate Zuishin''' Equipment Staff (commonly said, Ikawanogawa Mei), Armored Shield and Shogyokukei, All Take Off''', Detained Kageji, Immediately Riding Hakuun, Returning Soten. It is said to be the place where {{ill|Futsunushi|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsu Okami}} took off his shield, which is depicted in </ref>, and is therefore the sacred place of ``Tatenui''. There are two legends about the origin of the name Kihara, but both tell that the area has been a rich forest since ancient times.

It has a deep relationship with {{ill|Ami Shrine|Q17191825|qid=Q17191825|lt=Takekiami Shrine}} due to its association with the sacred place of Futsu mythology, and in ancient times it was called Ichinomiya Ninomiya as the main shrine for east and west Shinta District, and both {{ill|Eiwa|Q1145780|qid=Q1145780|lt=Eiwa}} 1st year (1375) of the Enmyin-ji Shrine and the Shrine and the Sobō Dojojo, which reads "Shonai Daiichi-no-Sobyo" <ref>Great Japanese Place Name Dictionary. </ref>. Tatenui Shrine was the Shinta District Ichinomiya Shrine, and was one of the most prestigious shrines in the former district area. An ancient ceremony (Kashima Shinto ritual) was also held in which the {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940}} of Futsu no Mikoto was carried to {{ill|Ami Shrine|Q16276818|qid=Q16276818}} via Lake Kasumigaura<ref name="keidai" />.

=== History ===
There is a company biography and a separate biography. In addition to the two theories about its founding, there is another theory that says it was built in 18 AD. </ref>.

=== Company biography ===
* Founded in {{ill|Empress Suiko|ar|الإمبراطورة سويكو|ast|Emperatriz Suiko|azb|امپراتریس سویکو|bcl|Emperatris Suiko|be|Імператрыца Суйка|ca|Suiko|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سویکۆ|cs|Suiko|de|Suiko|es|Suiko Tennō|eu|Suiko|fa|امپراتریس سوئیکو|fi|Suiko|fr|Suiko|hak|Suiko Thiên-fòng|he|סויקו, קיסרית יפן|hu|Szuiko japán császárnő|id|Suiko|it|Suiko|ja|推古天皇|ka|სუიკო|ko|스이코 천황|la|Suiko (imperatrix)|nl|Suiko|pl|Suiko|pt|Suiko|ru|Императрица Суйко|sh|Carica Suiko|simple|Empress Suiko|sl|Cesarica Suiko|sv|Suiko|ta|பேரரசி சுய்கோ|th|จักรพรรดินีซูอิโกะ|tl|Emperatris Suiko|tr|Suiko (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператор Суйко|uz|Imperator Suiko|vi|Thiên hoàng Suiko|zh|推古天皇|zh_classical|推古天皇|zh_min_nan|Suiko Thian-hông|zh_yue|推古天皇|qid=Q298057}}16 (608)<ref name="keidai">Precinct information board. </ref>.
* Searching for the auspicious origin of creation rituals in Fudu mythology. It is said that after the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=pacification of Ashihara China}}, Futsu Okami took off his armor at Kihara and ascended to heaven at Takakiri. Because he took off his armor, the place name ``Tatezu'' was born, and later became ``Tatenui.'' The place name ``Tatezuzan'' still remains on the shrine grounds.
* The name of the village of Kihara is derived from {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|cs|Eišó|fa|ایشو (دوره موروماچی)|fr|Ère Eishō (Muromachi)|ja|永正|ko|에이쇼 (센고쿠 시대)|no|Eishō (Sengoku)|ru|Эйсё|simple|Eishō (Muromachi period)|sr|Еишо (Муромачи период)|sv|Eishō (Sengoku)|tr|Eishō (Muromachi)|zh|永正|qid=Q1193577}} 3rd year (1506), which was built in the precincts of a temple with a circumference of 5 jo, 8 shaku, and a height of 120 shaku.{{jalink |Sugi|Q147388|Cedar}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} withered in May 1868) and {{ill|Kihara Castle|es|Castillo Kihara|ja|木原城 (常陸国)|qid=Q11518195|lt=Kihara Castle}}It was born by {{ill|combined|ja|合成地名|qid=Q11412460|lt=combined}} of the ``Hara'' of the lord Kondo Shikibu Daisuke Fujiwara Toshikatsu (Kondo Toshikatsu). Until then, it was called Kamikoshi Village.<ref>Precinct information board, Meiji Shrine magazine materials, etc. According to the Miho Village Board of Education's explanation of the cultural property, the origin is a giant cedar tree with a circumference of more than 6 meters located in the north of the precincts. </ref>.

=== Separate story ===
* The new edition of Hitachi Kokushi states, ``He is said to be the enshrined deity {{ill|Hikosachi no Mikoto|ja|彦狭知命|qid=Q135327097}}, the guardian of 33 villages in the Middle East of the district, and Ichinomiya of Sokuhon District (shaki, 28 shrines, 28 shrines summary origin) , this god was known as Amaterasu, the ancestor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ibe}} of {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}, as well as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tegiho Negami}}, during the age of the gods. For the great god |Q455602}}, he built a magnificent palace and made various ritual vessels to serve, but since this god only sewed shields, {{jalink|shield sewing|Q11582552|shield sewing} }}It is also said to be a god (Nihongi, Kogo Shui) <ref>Even in the human era, there was a tatebe who made shields for ritual utensils.</ref>'' (original kana), and the shrine is said to enshrine Hikosa Tomomichi, the ``tatenui deity.''
* The name of the village of Kihara is said to be from an ancient legend that says, ``In the old ancient times, this place was a vast wasteland, with cedar and cypress trees growing here and there, hence the name Kihara.One day, an old man suddenly appeared and told the villagers, ``Your houses are very poor, and when you see this palace, you should build one.'' The old man went under the shade of a cedar tree, entered Tamahinu, followed the worship of the villagers, gathered in front of the shrine, and started his home in this village (28 shrines abbreviated engagement)' (original kana), and it is also said that the Kihara village was formed along with Tatenui Shrine.
* In the local history of Inashiki District, there is a statement that says, ``Before the Meiji Restoration, there was a theory that people visited Tatenui Shrine and worshiped it, calling it the ancestral deity of carpenters,'' which suggests that a separate legend had spread in its own way until before the Meiji period.
*Generally, the deity enshrined at the shrine called Tatenui Shrine is Hikono Tomomichi. In addition to our company, there were at least four other Tatenui Shrines or Tatebe Shikinai shrines, all of which were shrines of the ``Tatenui God'' (Hikono Chimei).** Tatenui Shrine ({{ill|Tajima Province|Q1053727|qid=Q1053727}}{{ill|Yabu district|Q11666859|qid=Q11666859|lt=Yabu District}}, small shrine). Yabu City, Hyogo Prefecture. Main enshrined deity, Hikono Tomomi
** Tatenui Shrine (Tajima Province {{ill|Keta district|Q21655271|qid=Q21655271|lt=Keta District}}, small shrine). Toyooka City, Hyogo Prefecture. Main enshrined deity, Hikono Tomomi
** Tatenui Shrine ({{ill|Tanba Province|Q954511|qid=Q954511}}{{ill|Hikami District, Hyōgo|ja|氷上郡|zh|冰上郡|qid=Q5760344}}, small shrine). Tamba City, Hyogo Prefecture. Main enshrined deity, Hikono Tomomi
** Kawauchi Tatanuhi Shrine (Tamba Province {{ill|Taki district|ja|多紀郡|zh|多紀郡|qid=Q11431006}}, small shrine). Tamba City, Hyogo Prefecture. Main enshrined deity: Amaterasu Omikami<br/> ``Tadatanohi'' is a corruption of ``Tatenui,'' and it is said that it was originally a shrine of Tatebe that enshrined Hikonochi no Mikoto.
* {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092|lt=Specially Selected Names of Gods}} states, ``If the shrine name of Tatenui is used now, it would be as if Hikosa Chi no Mikoto could be enshrined; In the article, ``Futunushi no Mikoto re-sewn the heavenly stone shield (Ame no Ihatate). Therefore, it is called ``Tatenui.'''' edited by Yukichi Takeda. </ref> Together with the editorial, it is written that the name ``Tatenui'' is not necessarily derived from ``Tatenui no Mikoto'' (Hikosatomo no Mikoto).

=== History ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinryo}} had over 53 towns, but in the first year of {{ill|Kōkoku|de|Kōkoku|fa|کوکوکو|fr|Ère Kōkoku|ja|興国|ko|고코쿠|ru|Кококу|simple|Kōkoku|sr|Кококу|sv|Kōkoku|th|โคโกะกุ|tr|Kōkoku|zh|興國 (日本)|qid=Q1143592}} (1340), it was invaded by Nobutsune, a subordinate of {{ill|Kō no Morofuyu|Q6455071|qid=Q6455071}} of {{ill|Northern Court|Q1201819|qid=Q1201819|lt=Northern Court}}, and became without a living.<ref name="keidai" />
* It is said that a wooden guardian dog (a cultural property designated by Miho Village) was dedicated to the <ref name="joyo"/> for the {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} years (1532-1555).
* There are records of reconstruction in {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}}8 (1476), {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}17 (1589), and {{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}}7 (1854)<ref name="keidai" />. The current main hall is said to have been built in Tensho 17 and donated by Toshikatsu Kondo.
* In early modern times, Shinta County Ichinomiya was called the shrine of more than 50 villages in the eastern half of Shinta County.
* {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6 (1873), ranked as a prefectural company.
* {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}In 1965, the temple of worship was burnt down and ancient documents were lost<ref name="joyo">Joyo Living. </ref>.

:* Located to the northeast of Shinta Castle Ruins, the area is also a candidate site for Shinta {{ill|Gunga (Japan)|Q11643230|qid=Q11643230}}.

=== Transportation ===
Take the JR Bus Kanto from JR Tsuchiura Station, get off at the "Gonaka" bus stop, and walk 10 minutes.
